label: IP-antibiotic 1
evidence_snippet: Jen et al. synthesized 12 IP-antibiotic candidates and reported that compound 1 inhibited multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae WHO Z with a MIC of 0.156 mg/L, making it twofold more potent than PBT2 in the preliminary Table 1 assay.
evidence_notes: Table 1 supplies the exact 5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxyquinoline 2-amine structure for compound 1, and the experimental section names it as 2-Amino-5,7-dichloroquinolin-8-ol. The structure was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A 2-amino-5,7-dichloroquinolin-8-ol with antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

label: IP-antibiotic 2
evidence_snippet: Jen et al. reported that IP-antibiotic compound 2 inhibited multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae WHO Z with a MIC of 0.156 mg/L, inhibited the tested CLSI, MS11, and WHO multidrug-resistant N. gonorrhoeae strains with MICs of 0.078 to 0.156 mg/L, and showed dose-dependent killing in an ex vivo cervical infection model.
evidence_notes: Table 1 supplies the exact 5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxyquinoline isobutyramide structure for compound 2, and the experimental section names it as N-(5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxyquinolin-2-yl)isobutyramide. The structure was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A 5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxyquinoline isobutyramide with antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

label: IP-antibiotic 3
evidence_snippet: Jen et al. reported that IP-antibiotic compound 3 inhibited multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae WHO Z with a MIC of 0.078 mg/L, was highly effective against tested N. gonorrhoeae strains at MICs of 0.078 to 0.156 mg/L, and showed rapid antibacterial activity against N. gonorrhoeae WHO Z at 0.078 mg/L.
evidence_notes: Table 1 supplies the exact 5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxyquinoline acetamide structure for compound 3; Scheme 1 confirms it as the R = CH3 amide from the same 8-benzyloxy-5,7-dichloroquinolin-2-amine intermediate. The structure was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A 5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxyquinoline acetamide with antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

definition: A 5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxyquinoline 4-methylbenzenesulfonamide with antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

label: Corramycin
evidence_snippet: Couturier et al. established Corramycin as a myxobacterial linear peptide, elucidated its absolute configuration, and reported anti-Gram-negative activity.
evidence_notes: RCSB BIRD PRD_002426 supplies the machine-readable standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and stereochemical SMILES for Corramycin.
definition: A myxobacterial linear peptide with antibacterial activity.

label: AFN-1252
evidence_snippet: Karlowsky et al. reported that AFN-1252 inhibited all tested clinical Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates, including methicillin-resistant isolates, at concentrations of 0.12 micrograms per milliliter or lower.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 10407120 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for AFN-1252.
definition: A FabI inhibitor with narrow-spectrum antistaphylococcal antibacterial activity.

label: 5-indanol
evidence_snippet: Yang et al. identified 5-indanol as the dominant antibacterial marker in Amomum tsaoko stem and leaf extract and reported bactericidal activity against Staphylococcus aureus.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 15118 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for 5-indanol.
definition: An indane phenol with antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus.

label: CDK9-IN-2
evidence_snippet: Yan et al. identified CDK9-IN-2 in an HPrK kinase activity screen and reported antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Streptococcus suis, other Gram-positive species, and mycoplasmas.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 49855228 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for CDK9-IN-2.
definition: A small-molecule HPrK inhibitor with antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria and mycoplasmas.

label: Abaucin
evidence_snippet: Liu et al. discovered abaucin in a deep-learning screen and reported narrow-spectrum antibacterial activity against Acinetobacter baumannii, including clinical isolates with intrinsic and acquired resistance mechanisms.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 10000456 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for abaucin.
definition: A spirocyclic substituted phenethylamine with narrow-spectrum antibacterial activity against Acinetobacter baumannii.

label: Orientin
evidence_snippet: Zai et al. reported orientin among six Terminalia flavonoids that inhibited growth of both methicillin- and beta-lactam-resistant bacterial pathogens.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 5281675 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for orientin.
definition: A flavonoid with antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

label: Isoorientin
evidence_snippet: Zai et al. reported isoorientin among six Terminalia flavonoids that inhibited growth of both methicillin- and beta-lactam-resistant bacterial pathogens.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 114776 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for isoorientin.
definition: A flavonoid with antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

label: Hispidulin

evidence_notes: PubChem CID 5281628 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for hispidulin.
definition: A flavonoid with antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

label: Vitexin

definition: A flavonoid with antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

label: Fisetin
evidence_snippet: Zai et al. reported fisetin among six Terminalia flavonoids that inhibited growth of both methicillin- and beta-lactam-resistant bacterial pathogens.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 5281614 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for fisetin.
definition: A flavonoid with antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacterial pathogens.

label: Ibipinabant
evidence_snippet: Dove et al. identified ibipinabant as the most potent anti-gonococcal hit in a 2,528-molecule screen, reported bactericidal activity against Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and measured a significant gonococcal-burden reduction in a mouse genital tract infection model.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 9826744 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for ibipinabant.
definition: A cannabinoid receptor 1 antagonist with antibacterial activity against Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

label: Cladribine
evidence_snippet: Liu et al. identified cladribine as a potential antimicrobial candidate against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, reported growth inhibition and bactericidal activity against clinical isolates, and measured reduced pulmonary bacterial burden in a mouse lung infection model.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 20279 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for cladribine.
definition: A synthetic purine analogue with antibacterial activity against carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae.

label: NSC348884
evidence_snippet: Zhang et al. identified NSC348884 as a benzimidazole analogue with direct antibacterial activity against carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, reported anti-biofilm activity, and measured reduced blood bacterial load in a mouse systemic infection model.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 335974 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for NSC348884.
definition: A benzimidazole analogue with antibacterial activity against carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacteria.

label: Uliginosin B
evidence_snippet: Scaffo et al. tested isolated uliginosin B against reference and drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates, reported MICs of 3.125 to 6.25 ug/mL and MBCs of 6.25 to 12.5 ug/mL, and linked exposure to oxidative stress.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 5315118 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for uliginosin B.
definition: A polyprenylated acylphloroglucinol with antibacterial activity against drug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

label: Genipin
evidence_snippet: Slenter et al. tested genipin against canine ocular Staphylococcus pseudintermedius, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Streptococcus canis isolates, reported minimum bactericidal concentrations, and measured concentration-dependent bactericidal activity against staphylococci.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 442424 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for genipin.
definition: An iridoid with antibacterial activity against canine ocular staphylococcal isolates.

label: Spinasterol
evidence_snippet: Birhanu et al. isolated spinasterol from Impatiens rothii tuber extract, identified it by MS and NMR, and measured antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Vibrio cholerae with MIC values of 25 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 5281331 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for spinasterol.
definition: A phytosterol with antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Vibrio cholerae.

label: Luteolin
evidence_snippet: Yang et al. reported that luteolin inhibited multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli with a MIC of 1 mg/mL and a MBC of 2 mg/mL, inhibited biofilm formation, disrupted bacterial cell integrity, and suppressed ATP synthesis.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 5280445 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for luteolin.
definition: A flavonoid with antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli.

label: Visomitin
evidence_snippet: Yang et al. reported that Visomitin had MIC values of 4 to 8 ug/mL and MBC values of 4 to 16 ug/mL against Enterococcus, showed time-dependent bactericidal activity, inhibited and partly eradicated biofilms, and reduced abscess size and bacterial load in a mouse subcutaneous abscess model.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 16679091 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for Visomitin.
definition: A plastoquinonyl-decyl-triphenylphosphonium bromide with antibacterial activity against Enterococcus.

label: PBT2
evidence_snippet: Jen et al. reported that PBT2 alone was sufficient to inhibit the growth of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and used that result to guide 8-hydroxyquinoline ionophoroantibiotics with potent activity against multidrug-resistant N. gonorrhoeae.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 10016012 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for PBT2.
definition: An 8-hydroxyquinoline zinc ionophore with antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

label: (S,S)-4-F-Phe-Ala
evidence_snippet: Dounay et al. reported that compound 11b, (S,S)-4-F-Phe-Ala, inhibited Pseudomonas aeruginosa growth with IC50 and IC90 values of 0.57 and 3.46 ug/mL and inhibited biofilm formation with IC50 and IC90 values of 0.36 and 2.95 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: Supplementary Scheme S1 and the characterization block for 11b supply the connectivity and stereochemistry used to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: An (S,S)-4-fluorophenylalanine-alanine dipeptide with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

label: ECF transporter inhibitor 36
evidence_snippet: Exapicheidou et al. reported that compound 36 inhibited Enterococcus faecalis, Enterococcus faecium, and Streptococcus pneumoniae strains with MIC values of 0.5 to 4 ug/mL and had an ECF-FolT2 IC50 of 42.84 uM in the Lactobacillus delbrueckii proteoliposome uptake assay.
evidence_notes: Supplementary Data CSV row 36 reports the SMILES for compound 36 and Scheme 5 supplies the same triazolyl derivative scaffold; the CSV SMILES was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A 1,4-triazole-pyridinyl salicylic acid derivative with antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.

label: ECF transporter inhibitor 3
evidence_snippet: Exapicheidou et al. reported that hit compound 3 inhibited Enterococcus faecalis DSM-20478 (MIC 11 ug/mL), Enterococcus faecium DSM-17050 (MIC 3 to 6 ug/mL), Enterococcus faecium DSM-20477 (MIC 11 ug/mL), Streptococcus pneumoniae DSM-11865 (MIC 6 ug/mL), and Streptococcus pneumoniae DSM-20566 (MIC 1 to 3 ug/mL) while inhibiting Lactobacillus casei vitamin uptake with an IC50 of 28 uM.
evidence_notes: Table 1 and the experimental section of PMC13312448 identify compound 3 as 5-((3,5-di-tert-butylbenzyl)oxy)-2-hydroxybenzoic acid; the structure was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A 5-((3,5-di-tert-butylbenzyl)oxy)-2-hydroxybenzoic acid ECF transporter inhibitor with antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.

label: ECF transporter inhibitor 18
evidence_snippet: Exapicheidou et al. reported that compound 18 inhibited Enterococcus faecalis, Enterococcus faecium, and Streptococcus pneumoniae strains with MIC values of 1 to 9 ug/mL, inhibited Lactobacillus casei vitamin uptake with an IC50 of 4 uM, and improved larval survival in a Galleria mellonella Streptococcus pneumoniae infection model.
evidence_notes: Supplementary Data CSV row 18 reports the SMILES for compound 18, matching PubChem CID 176360086; the SMILES was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A bis(5-chloro-6-isopropoxypyridin-3-yl)benzyloxy salicylic acid ECF transporter inhibitor with antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.

label: ECF transporter inhibitor 31
evidence_snippet: Exapicheidou et al. reported that compound 31 inhibited Enterococcus faecalis, Enterococcus faecium, and Streptococcus pneumoniae strains with MIC values of 0.5 to 2 ug/mL and inhibited Lactobacillus casei vitamin uptake with an IC50 of 5 uM.
evidence_notes: Supplementary Data CSV row 31 reports the SMILES for compound 31, matching PubChem CID 176359509; the SMILES was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A cyclopentyl-triazolyl-pyridinyl salicylic acid ECF transporter inhibitor with antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.

label: ECF transporter inhibitor 33
evidence_snippet: Exapicheidou et al. reported that compound 33 inhibited Enterococcus faecalis, Enterococcus faecium, and Streptococcus pneumoniae strains with MIC values of 0.3 to 4.5 ug/mL, inhibited Lactobacillus casei vitamin uptake with an IC50 of 4 uM, and improved larval survival in a Galleria mellonella Streptococcus pneumoniae infection model.
evidence_notes: Supplementary Data CSV row 33 reports the SMILES for compound 33, matching PubChem CID 176360252; the SMILES was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A thiophen-3-yl-triazolyl-pyridinyl salicylic acid ECF transporter inhibitor with antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.

label: ECF transporter inhibitor 34
evidence_snippet: Exapicheidou et al. reported that compound 34 inhibited Enterococcus faecalis, Enterococcus faecium, and Streptococcus pneumoniae strains with MIC values of 0.6 to 2 ug/mL and inhibited Lactobacillus casei vitamin uptake with an IC50 of 4 uM.
evidence_notes: Supplementary Data CSV row 34 reports the SMILES for compound 34 and Scheme 5 supplies the same thiophen-2-yl triazolyl salicylic acid scaffold; the SMILES was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A thiophen-2-yl-triazolyl-pyridinyl salicylic acid ECF transporter inhibitor with antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria.

label: 4-Fluoro-L-phenylalanine
evidence_snippet: Dounay et al. reported that compound 3, (S)-4-F-Phe, inhibited Pseudomonas aeruginosa PA14 planktonic growth with IC50 and IC90 values of 0.42 and 1.24 ug/mL and inhibited biofilm formation with IC50 and IC90 values of 0.26 and 0.84 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 716312 and ChEBI CHEBI:44909 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for 4-fluoro-L-phenylalanine ((S)-4-F-Phe, compound 3).
definition: A fluorinated L-phenylalanine analogue with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

label: NOSO-502
evidence_snippet: Racine et al. evaluated the odilorhabdin antibiotic NOSO-502 and reported that MexXY-OprM efflux-deficient Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains (PAO750, 11B, PAO1T, and PAO1 delta-mexXY) were susceptible to NOSO-502 with MIC values of 2 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 121246383 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for NOSO-502.
definition: A synthetic odilorhabdin peptide antibiotic that inhibits the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit and has antibacterial activity against Enterobacterales and efflux-deficient Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

label: Dehydro-delta-viniferin
evidence_snippet: Johnsen et al. reported that dehydro-delta-viniferin inhibited methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus USA300 and cefoxitin-treated USA300Cef with a MIC of 2 ug/mL and MBC values of 8 to 16 ug/mL while enhancing IL-12 production in MRSA-stimulated dendritic cells.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 141762088 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for dehydro-delta-viniferin.
definition: A resveratrol dehydrodimer stilbenoid with bactericidal activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

label: Viniferifuran
evidence_snippet: Johnsen et al. reported that viniferifuran inhibited methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus USA300 and cefoxitin-treated USA300Cef with a MIC of 8 ug/mL and MBC values of 32 to 64 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 131751470 and ChEBI CHEBI:180720 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for viniferifuran.
definition: A benzofuran resveratrol dimer stilbenoid with antibacterial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

label: Kaempferol 3-O-gentiobioside
evidence_snippet: Samir et al. isolated kaempferol 3-O-gentiobioside from Solanum muricatum aerial parts and reported anti-MRSA activity with a MIC of 8.3 uM and MBC of 16.5 uM, 70.11% biofilm inhibition at 1/2 MIC, and synergy with gentamicin (FICI 0.285).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 9960512 and ChEBI CHEBI:136785 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for kaempferol 3-O-gentiobioside.
definition: A kaempferol O-diglycoside flavonoid with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

label: Kaempferol 3-O-sambubioside
evidence_snippet: Samir et al. isolated kaempferol 3-O-sambubioside from Solanum muricatum aerial parts and reported anti-MRSA activity with a MIC of 10.2 uM and MBC of 20.4 uM, 75.09% biofilm inhibition at 1/2 MIC, and synergy with gentamicin (FICI 0.413).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 44566720 and ChEBI CHEBI:189496 (leucoside) supply the fully stereodefined standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for kaempferol 3-O-beta-D-sambubioside.
definition: A kaempferol O-diglycoside flavonoid with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

label: Trichorzianine 1938
evidence_snippet: Chen et al. isolated trichorzianine 1938 from marine-derived Trichoderma longibrachiatum ST-27 and reported antibacterial activity against the aquaculture pathogen Vibrio harveyi VH306 with a MIC of 300 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: Table 5 of DOI:10.3390/ijms27177714 explicitly cites PubChem CID 163114856 for trichorzianine 1938, supplying the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES (with the C-91 isovaline stereocenter left unassigned in the primary source).
definition: A 19-residue fungal peptaibol with antibacterial activity against Vibrio harveyi.

label: Asiatic acid
evidence_snippet: Maitra et al. reported that asiatic acid inhibited Shigella flexneri Sf2457T and multidrug-resistant clinical strain BCH12654 in a dose-dependent manner, reduced biofilm viability and AcrAB-TolC efflux pump expression, and lowered bacterial burden in vivo.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 119034 and ChEBI CHEBI:2873 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for asiatic acid.
definition: An ursane-type pentacyclic triterpenoid with antibacterial, antibiofilm, and efflux-inhibitory activity against Shigella flexneri.

label: Pantoprazole
evidence_snippet: Salcedo-Sora and Kell identified the benzimidazole proton-pump inhibitor pantoprazole as a top hit in a flow-cytometric Prestwick library membrane-permeabilization screen and reported growth inhibition (Fig. 7a-b median IC50 across the three validated hits: 0.57 to 0.59 mg/L against Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 and 0.68 to 0.72 mg/L against Escherichia coli BW25113).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 4679 and ChEBI CHEBI:7915 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for pantoprazole.
definition: A substituted benzimidazole sulfoxide proton-pump inhibitor with bactericidal membrane-permeabilizing activity against Acinetobacter baylyi and Escherichia coli.

label: Theophylline
evidence_snippet: Salcedo-Sora and Kell validated pure theophylline following the Prestwick library aminophylline hit in a flow-cytometric membrane-permeabilization screen and reported growth inhibition (Fig. 7a-b median IC50 across the three validated hits: 0.57 to 0.59 mg/L against Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 and 0.68 to 0.72 mg/L against Escherichia coli BW25113).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 2153 and ChEBI CHEBI:28177 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for theophylline.
definition: A 1,3-dimethylxanthine with bactericidal membrane-permeabilizing activity against Acinetobacter baylyi and Escherichia coli.

label: Zoledronic acid
evidence_snippet: Salcedo-Sora and Kell identified the nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate zoledronic acid as a top hit in a flow-cytometric Prestwick library membrane-permeabilization screen and reported growth inhibition (Fig. 7a-b median IC50 across the three validated hits: 0.57 to 0.59 mg/L against Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 and 0.68 to 0.72 mg/L against Escherichia coli BW25113).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 68740 and ChEBI CHEBI:46557 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for zoledronic acid.
definition: An imidazole-containing bisphosphonate with bactericidal membrane-permeabilizing activity against Acinetobacter baylyi and Escherichia coli.

label: Broxyquinoline
evidence_snippet: Mendez et al. reported that broxyquinoline inhibited in vivo bacterial cytochrome c biogenesis System I (reducing heme signal to 28% of wild type at 7.5 uM) and demonstrated antibacterial zone-of-inhibition activity across tested bacterial species.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 2453 and ChEBI CHEBI:109543 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for broxyquinoline.
definition: A 5,7-dibromoquinolin-8-ol with antibacterial activity that inhibits bacterial cytochrome c maturation in vivo.

label: Pyrithione zinc
evidence_snippet: Mendez et al. reported that pyrithione zinc inhibited in vivo cytochrome c biogenesis System I and System II (reducing heme signals to 14% and 12% of wild type at 7.5 uM) and demonstrated strong broad-spectrum antibacterial zone-of-inhibition activity across six bacterial species.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 26041 and ChEBI CHEBI:32076 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for pyrithione zinc (the 2:1 Zn(II) coordination complex of pyrithione, CHEBI:8647).
definition: A zinc coordination complex of pyrithione (CHEBI:8647) with broad-spectrum antibacterial and antifungal activity.

label: Phenylmercuric acetate
evidence_snippet: Mendez et al. reported that phenylmercuric acetate inhibited in vivo cytochrome c biogenesis System I and System II (reducing heme signals to 10% and 2% of wild type at 7.5 uM) and demonstrated strong antibacterial zone-of-inhibition activity across six tested bacterial species.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 16682730 and ChEBI CHEBI:27684 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for phenylmercuric acetate.
definition: An organomercury compound with antibacterial and antifungal activity that inhibits bacterial cytochrome c biogenesis in vivo.

label: Caffeic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that caffeic acid inhibited 9 of 10 tested wound-associated bacterial strains at a MIC of 2.5 mg/mL and Escherichia coli ATCC 35218 at 5.0 mg/mL (Table 1), showed bactericidal activity with MBCs of 2.5 to 5.0 mg/mL (Table 2), and induced filamentation in planktonic Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 689043 and ChEBI CHEBI:16433 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for caffeic acid.
definition: A 3,4-dihydroxycinnamic acid with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Chlorogenic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that chlorogenic acid inhibited Staphylococcus epidermidis ATCC 12228 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 at a MIC of 5.0 mg/mL and the remaining 8 tested wound-associated strains at 10.0 mg/mL (Table 1), had MBC values of 5.0 to 10.0 mg/mL (Table 2), and induced filamentation in planktonic Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 1794427 and ChEBI CHEBI:16112 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for chlorogenic acid.
definition: A caffeoylquinic acid ester with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: p-Coumaric acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that p-coumaric acid inhibited Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 at a MIC of 0.625 mg/mL, Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Klebsiella quasipneumoniae, and Klebsiella pneumoniae at 1.25 mg/mL, and Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Proteus mirabilis at 2.5 mg/mL (Table 1), with uniform MBCs of 2.5 mg/mL across all 10 strains (Table 2).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 637542 and ChEBI CHEBI:32374 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for p-coumaric acid.
definition: A 4-hydroxycinnamic acid with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Ferulic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that ferulic acid inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538 and Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 at a MIC of 1.25 mg/mL, Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC 27853 at 5.0 mg/mL, and the remaining 7 wound-associated strains at 2.5 mg/mL (Table 1), with MBCs of 2.5 to 5.0 mg/mL (Table 2).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 445858 and ChEBI CHEBI:17620 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for ferulic acid.
definition: A 4-hydroxy-3-methoxycinnamic acid with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Rosmarinic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that rosmarinic acid inhibited 8 of 10 tested wound-associated bacterial strains at a MIC of 5.0 mg/mL and Escherichia coli ATCC 35218 and Klebsiella pneumoniae ATCC 10031 at 10.0 mg/mL (Table 1), with MBC values of 5.0 to 10.0 mg/mL (Table 2).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 5281792 and ChEBI CHEBI:50371 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for rosmarinic acid.
definition: A caffeic acid ester of salvianic acid A with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Gallic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that gallic acid inhibited Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC 27853 at a MIC of 2.5 mg/mL, Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25923 at 10.0 mg/mL, and the remaining 7 wound-associated strains at 5.0 mg/mL (Table 1), with MBCs of 5.0 to 10.0 mg/mL (Table 2).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 370 and ChEBI CHEBI:30778 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for gallic acid.
definition: A 3,4,5-trihydroxybenzoic acid with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Syringic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that syringic acid inhibited 7 of 10 tested wound-associated bacterial strains at a MIC of 2.5 mg/mL and Escherichia coli ATCC 35218, Klebsiella quasipneumoniae ATCC 700603, and Klebsiella pneumoniae ATCC 10031 at 5.0 mg/mL (Table 1), with MBCs of 2.5 to 5.0 mg/mL (Table 2).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 10742 and ChEBI CHEBI:68329 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for syringic acid.
definition: A 4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxybenzoic acid with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Vanillic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that vanillic acid inhibited Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 6538 at a MIC of 1.25 mg/mL and the remaining 9 tested wound-associated bacterial strains at 2.5 mg/mL (Table 1), with MBC values of 2.5 to 5.0 mg/mL (Table 2).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 8468 and ChEBI CHEBI:30816 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for vanillic acid.
definition: A 4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzoic acid with bactericidal and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Quinic acid
evidence_snippet: Barzdina et al. reported that quinic acid inhibited Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 and Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC 27853 at a MIC of 2.5 mg/mL and the remaining 8 tested wound-associated bacterial strains at 5.0 mg/mL (Table 1), with MBC values of 2.5 to 5.0 mg/mL (Table 2).
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 6508 and ChEBI CHEBI:17521 (CAS 77-95-2) supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for D-(-)-quinic acid.
definition: A tetrahydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid with antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against wound-associated bacterial pathogens.

label: Thiocolchicoside
evidence_snippet: Devi and Khanwelkar reported that thiocolchicoside inhibited Streptococcus mutans, Staphylococcus aureus, Lactobacillus acidophilus, Escherichia coli, and Candida albicans with MICs of 125 ug/mL, Aspergillus niger at 250 ug/mL, and Klebsiella pneumoniae at 500 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 9915886 and ChEBI CHEBI:94557 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for thiocolchicoside.
definition: A semi-synthetic sulfur-substituted colchicoside derivative with antibacterial and antifungal activity.

label: Deferoxamine
evidence_snippet: Lira et al. reported that deferoxamine inhibited Mycobacterium abscessus subsp. massiliense with a bacteriostatic MIC of 9.75 ug/mL, showed strong synergy with clarithromycin (FICI 0.047), reduced biofilm biomass, and lowered intracellular bacterial burden in infected RAW 264.7 macrophages.
evidence_notes: PubChem CID 2973 and ChEBI CHEBI:4356 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for deferoxamine.
definition: A bacterial tris-hydroxamate siderophore and iron chelator with antimycobacterial and antibiofilm activity against Mycobacterium abscessus.

label: lolamicin
evidence_snippet: The resultant compound—lolamicin—is selectively active against a panel of more than 130 multidrug-resistant clinical isolates, has efficacy in multiple mouse models of acute pneumonia and septicaemia infection, and spares the gut microbiome in mice, preventing secondary infection with Clostridioides difficile.
evidence_notes: Reported by Munoz et al. 2024 (Nature 630:429-436; PMID:38811738) as a Gram-negative-specific inhibitor of the LolCDE outer-membrane lipoprotein transport complex that spares commensal gut bacteria, with MIC 1-2 ug/mL against Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates (MIC50/MIC90 1/2 mg/L for E. coli and 1/4 mg/L for K. pneumoniae in DOI:10.1128/aac.01701-25).
definition: A 3,4-diaryl-1H-pyrazole antibacterial that selectively inhibits the LolCDE lipoprotein transport complex in pathogenic Gram-negative Enterobacterales while sparing gut commensals.

label: cresomycin
evidence_snippet: On the basis of structural analyses of bacterial ribosomes bound to diverse antibiotics, we designed a conformationally restricted molecule, which we name cresomycin (CRM), that adopts the exact conformation required for ribosomal binding. CRM exhibits potent in vitro and in vivo efficacy against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including multidrug-resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
evidence_notes: Reported by Wu et al. 2024 (Science 383:721-726; PMID:38359125) as a conformationally preorganized bridged macrobicyclic oxepanoprolinamide antibiotic targeting the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl transferase center, exhibiting MICs of <=0.06-0.25 ug/mL against multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (including cfr- and erm-positive strains), 1-2 ug/mL against Escherichia coli, and in vivo murine septicemia and thigh-infection efficacy.
definition: A synthetic bridged macrobicyclic oxepanoprolinamide antibiotic preorganized for binding to the bacterial 50S ribosomal peptidyl transferase center and active against multidrug-resistant Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

label: fabimycin
evidence_snippet: This compound, which we have named fabimycin, displays impressive activity against >200 clinical isolates of E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and A. baumannii, does not kill commensal bacteria indiscriminately, and demonstrates efficacy in multiple mouse models of infection caused by Gram-negative bacteria.
evidence_notes: Reported by Parker et al. 2022 (ACS Cent Sci 8:1145-1158; PMID:36035943) as an eNTRy-rule-optimized primary-amine-bearing enoyl-ACP reductase (FabI) inhibitor active against >200 clinical isolates of Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Acinetobacter baumannii (typical MICs 1-4 ug/mL; confirmed at MIC 2 ug/mL against K. pneumoniae ATCC 43816 in DOI:10.1021/acsinfecdis.3c00391).
definition: A pyrido[2,3-b]azepinone-linked tetrahydro-1,8-naphthyridine antibacterial that accumulates in Gram-negative bacteria and inhibits the fatty acid biosynthesis enzyme enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (FabI).

label: ibezapolstat
evidence_snippet: Ibezapolstat is a novel DNA polymerase IIIC inhibitor structural class under clinical development for the treatment of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). In the 28 RT027 strains, the MIC50, MIC90, and geometric mean MIC values were 2.0, 4.0, and 2.1 ug/mL for ibezapolstat.
evidence_notes: Reported by Murray et al. 2024 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 68:e0033224; PMID:38717162) as a dichlorobenzyl-substituted guanine analogue (ACX-362E) that selectively inhibits low-G+C Gram-positive bacterial DNA polymerase IIIC (PolC), with MIC50 = 2.0 ug/mL and MIC90 = 4.0 ug/mL against clinical Clostridioides difficile isolates.
definition: A 7-(2-morpholin-4-ylethyl)-N2-(3,4-dichlorobenzyl)guanine antibacterial that inhibits bacterial DNA polymerase IIIC (PolC) in Clostridioides difficile and other Firmicutes.

label: manogepix
evidence_snippet: Fosmanogepix is a novel broad-spectrum antifungal agent currently in phase 3 clinical trials. Its active moiety, manogepix (MGX), inhibits the fungal enzyme Gwt1, a conserved glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored wall transfer protein essential for fungal cell wall integrity. MGX displayed uniform potent in vitro activity, with minimal effective concentration (MEC) values ranging from <=0.008 to 0.03 ug/mL (modal MEC, <=0.008 ug/mL; MEC50, <=0.008 ug/mL; MEC90, 0.015 ug/mL) for E. africanum.
evidence_notes: Reported by Maphanga et al. 2026 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother; PMID:42206792) and Pfaller et al. 2023 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 67:e0084923; DOI:10.1128/aac.00849-23) as the active antifungal moiety (APX001A, E1210) of fosmanogepix targeting fungal glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored wall transfer protein 1 (Gwt1), with MEC50/MEC90 <=0.008/0.015 ug/mL against dimorphic fungi and MIC50/MIC90 0.008/0.06 mg/L across Candida species.
definition: An isoxazolylpyridinamine antifungal agent (active moiety of the prodrug fosmanogepix) that inhibits fungal inositol acyltransferase Gwt1 and blocks glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored mannoprotein maturation.

label: olorofim
evidence_snippet: Olorofim is a first-in-class orotomide antifungal agent that acts via inhibition of the pyrimidine biosynthesis enzyme dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH). Olorofim showed potent in vitro activity against A. fumigatus (n = 1,031; MIC50/90, 0.03/0.06 mg/L; 100% WT), including itraconazole-non-wild-type (NWT; n = 98; MIC50/90, 0.03/0.06 mg/L) and voriconazole-NWT (n = 55; MIC50/90, 0.03/0.06 mg/L) isolates.
evidence_notes: Reported by Pfaller et al. 2023 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 67:e0030723; PMID:37338411) as a first-in-class orotomide pyrrole-2-yl-2-oxoacetamide antifungal (F901318) that inhibits fungal dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH), showing MIC50/MIC90 of 0.03/0.06 mg/L across 1,031 clinical Aspergillus fumigatus isolates.
definition: A first-in-class orotomide antifungal agent that selectively inhibits fungal mitochondrial dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) in de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis.

label: ibrexafungerp
evidence_snippet: Ibrexafungerp is a first-in-class oral triterpenoid glucan synthase inhibitor. Ibrexafungerp showed potent in vitro activity against Candida albicans (n = 166; MIC50/90, 0.06/0.25 mg/L), Candida parapsilosis (n = 123; MIC50/90, 0.5/1 mg/L), Candida glabrata (n = 68; MIC50/90, 0.25/1 mg/L), Candida tropicalis (n = 45; MIC50/90, 0.25/1 mg/L), and Candida krusei (n = 15; MIC50/90, 0.5/1 mg/L), including fluconazole- and echinocandin-resistant isolates.
evidence_notes: Reported by Mesquida et al. 2022 (Med Mycol 60:myac049; PMID:35816437) as a semisynthetic enfumafungin-derived triterpenoid 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase inhibitor (SCY-078, MK-3118) with MIC50/MIC90 of 0.06/0.25 mg/L against Candida albicans and 0.25/1 mg/L against Candida glabrata bloodstream isolates.
definition: A semisynthetic enfumafungin-derived triterpenoid antifungal agent (fungerp class) that inhibits fungal 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase (Fks1/Fks2) and disrupts fungal cell wall assembly.

label: oteseconazole
evidence_snippet: Oteseconazole (VT-1161) is a novel fungal CYP51 inhibitor specifically designed to selectively target the fungal enzyme over human cytochrome P450 enzymes. Against C. glabrata clinical isolates, VT-1161 MICs ranged from <=0.015 to 2 ug/mL (MIC50, 0.06 ug/mL; MIC90, 0.5 ug/mL), and against C. krusei isolates, VT-1161 MICs ranged from 0.03 to 0.5 ug/mL (MIC50, 0.12 ug/mL; MIC90, 0.25 ug/mL).
evidence_notes: Reported by Nishimoto et al. 2022 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 66:e0077822; PMID:35969069) as a selective tetrazole inhibitor (VT-1161) of fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51), with MIC50/MIC90 of 0.06/0.5 ug/mL against Candida glabrata and 0.12/0.25 ug/mL against Candida krusei clinical isolates.
definition: A tetrazole antifungal agent that selectively coordinates the heme iron of fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51) to block ergosterol biosynthesis.

label: ridinilazole
evidence_snippet: Ridinilazole (RDZ) is a narrow-spectrum bis-benzimidazole antibacterial agent developed for the treatment of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). Across all 304 baseline C. difficile isolates collected in the Phase 3 Ri-CoDIFy trials, ridinilazole demonstrated potent in vitro activity with an MIC50 of 0.125 mg/L, an MIC90 of 0.25 mg/L, and an MIC range of 0.03 to 0.5 mg/L.
evidence_notes: Reported by Basseres et al. 2024 (J Antimicrob Chemother 79:1906-1914; PMID:38775229) as a narrow-spectrum symmetrical bis-benzimidazole antibacterial (SMT19969) that binds the DNA minor groove and impairs bacterial septum formation, with MIC50/MIC90 of 0.125/0.25 mg/L across 304 Phase 3 Clostridioides difficile clinical isolates.
definition: A symmetrical 2,2'-bis(pyridin-4-yl)-1H,1'H-5,5'-bibenzimidazole narrow-spectrum antibacterial agent active against Clostridioides difficile.

label: delpazolid
evidence_snippet: Delpazolid (LCB01-0371) is a novel oxazolidinone with cyclic amidrazone under clinical investigation. Against clinical M. tuberculosis isolates, delpazolid showed an MIC50 of 0.5 mg/L and an MIC90 of 1.0 mg/L. Against M. abscessus isolates, delpazolid exhibited an MIC50 of 2.0 mg/L and an MIC90 of 4.0 mg/L.
evidence_notes: Reported by Shang et al. 2024 (Int J Antimicrob Agents 64:107242; PMID:38909850) as a cyclic-amidrazone-bearing oxazolidinone antibacterial (LCB01-0371) targeting the 50S ribosomal subunit, exhibiting MIC50/MIC90 of 0.5/1.0 mg/L against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and 2.0/4.0 mg/L against Mycobacterium abscessus clinical isolates.
definition: An oxazolidinone antibacterial incorporating a cyclic amidrazone C-ring that inhibits bacterial protein synthesis at the 50S ribosomal subunit with potent antimycobacterial and anti-Gram-positive activity.

label: epetraborole
evidence_snippet: Epetraborole is a boron-containing leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LeuRS) inhibitor under clinical development for treatment-refractory Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) lung disease. Epetraborole inhibited 99.3% of M. avium complex isolates at <=4 ug/mL (MIC50/90, 1/2 ug/mL) and 100.0% of M. abscessus isolates at <=0.5 ug/mL (MIC50/90, 0.12/0.25 ug/mL).
evidence_notes: Reported by Castanheira et al. 2023 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 67:e0102923; PMID:37937988) as a benzoxaborole inhibitor (AN3365, GSK2251052) of bacterial leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LeuRS) via oxaborole-assisted tRNA(Leu) trapping in the editing domain, with MIC50/MIC90 of 1/2 ug/mL against Mycobacterium avium complex and 0.12/0.25 ug/mL against Mycobacterium abscessus.
definition: A 3-aminomethylbenzoxaborole antibacterial agent that inhibits bacterial leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LeuRS) by forming a covalent adduct with the terminal adenosine of tRNA(Leu) in the editing site.

label: ganfeborole
evidence_snippet: Ganfeborole (GSK3036656) is a first-in-class benzoxaborole inhibiting Mycobacterium tuberculosis leucyl-tRNA synthetase. Ganfeborole exhibits potent in vitro activity against M. tuberculosis H37Rv (MIC = 0.08 uM; ~0.024 ug/mL) and demonstrated bactericidal early bactericidal activity in patients with rifampicin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis at oral doses of 10-30 mg once daily.
evidence_notes: Reported by Diacon et al. 2024 (Nat Med 30:896-904; PMID:38365949) as a 4-chlorobenzoxaborole inhibitor (GSK3036656, GSK656) of Mycobacterium tuberculosis leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LeuRS), with an M. tuberculosis H37Rv MIC of 0.08 uM (~0.024 ug/mL) and clinical bactericidal efficacy in Phase 2a tuberculosis patients.
definition: A 4-chloro-3-aminomethylbenzoxaborole antitubercular agent that selectively inhibits Mycobacterium tuberculosis leucyl-tRNA synthetase (LeuRS).

label: quabodepistat
evidence_snippet: OPC-167832 (quabodepistat) is a newly synthesized 3,4-dihydrocarbostyril derivative targeting decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-oxidase (DprE1). The MICs of OPC-167832 for M. tuberculosis laboratory and clinical isolates ranged from 0.00024 to 0.001 ug/mL, and its 50% inhibitory concentration (IC50) against recombinant M. tuberculosis DprE1 was 0.258 uM.
evidence_notes: Reported by Hariguchi et al. 2022 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 66:e0033822; PMID:35699441) and Hariguchi et al. 2020 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 64:e02020-19; DOI:10.1128/aac.02020-19) as a noncovalent 3,4-dihydrocarbostyril inhibitor (OPC-167832) of Mycobacterium tuberculosis decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-oxidase (DprE1, IC50 = 0.258 uM) with MICs of 0.00024-0.001 ug/mL across drug-susceptible and multidrug-resistant M. tuberculosis isolates.
definition: A 3,4-dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-one (3,4-dihydrocarbostyril) antitubercular agent that inhibits mycobacterial decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-oxidase (DprE1) and cell wall arabinogalactan synthesis.

label: telacebec
evidence_snippet: Here, we report on a promising class of imidazopyridine amide (IPA) compounds that block Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth by targeting the respiratory cytochrome bc1 complex. The optimized IPA compound Q203 inhibited the growth of MDR and XDR M. tuberculosis clinical isolates in culture broth medium in the low nanomolar range and was efficacious in a mouse model of tuberculosis at a dose less than 1 mg per kg body weight.
evidence_notes: Reported by Pethe et al. 2013 (Nat Med 19:1157-1160; PMID:23913123) as an imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine-3-carboxamide (Q203) targeting the QcrB subunit of the mycobacterial respiratory cytochrome bc1:aa3 complex, with MIC50 = 2.7 nM (~1.5 ng/mL) against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv in broth and MIC50 = 0.28 nM inside macrophages.
definition: An imidazo[1,2-a]pyridine-3-carboxamide antimycobacterial agent (Q203) that inhibits the QcrB subunit of the respiratory cytochrome bc1:aa3 complex and depletes mycobacterial ATP.

label: macozinone
evidence_snippet: Here, we synthesized a new series of piperazine-containing benzothiazinones (PBTZ) and show that, like BTZ043, the preclinical candidate PBTZ169 binds covalently to DprE1. The crystal structure of the DprE1-PBTZ169 complex reveals formation of a semimercaptal adduct with Cys387 in the active site and explains the irreversible inactivation of the enzyme.
evidence_notes: Reported by Makarov et al. 2014 (EMBO Mol Med 6:372-383; PMID:24500695) as a 2-[4-(cyclohexylmethyl)piperazin-1-yl]-8-nitro-6-(trifluoromethyl)-1,3-benzothiazin-4-one (PBTZ169) that covalently modifies Cys387 of Mycobacterium tuberculosis decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-epimerase (DprE1) and inhibits M. tuberculosis H37Rv growth at MIC <= 0.19 ng/mL (0.4 nM).
definition: A piperazine-substituted 8-nitro-1,3-benzothiazin-4-one antitubercular agent (PBTZ169) that undergoes nitro-to-nitroso bioreduction and forms a covalent semimercaptal adduct with Cys387 of mycobacterial DprE1.

label: luliconazole
evidence_snippet: Luliconazole inhibited growth of all filamentous fungi except zygomycetes at low concentrations (MIC, < or =0.004-0.125 microg/ml), with dermatophytes being most susceptible (MIC, < or =0.004-0.008 microg/ml). yeastlike fungi were also susceptible to luliconazole (MIC, 0.125-4 microg/ml).
evidence_notes: Reported by Uchida et al. 2004 (J Infect Chemother 10:216-219; PMID:15365862) as an optically active R-enantiomer ketene dithioacetal imidazole antifungal (NND-502) inhibiting fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, with MICs of <=0.004-0.008 ug/mL against Trichophyton dermatophytes and 0.125-4 ug/mL against Candida species.
definition: An optically active (2E)-2-[(4R)-4-(2,4-dichlorophenyl)-1,3-dithiolan-2-ylidene]-2-(1H-imidazol-1-yl)acetonitrile antifungal agent that inhibits fungal sterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51).

label: thermorubin A
evidence_snippet: Thermorubin (THR) is an aromatic anthracenopyranone antibiotic active against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. It is known to bind to the 70S ribosome at the intersubunit bridge B2a and was thought to inhibit factor-dependent initiation of translation and obstruct the accommodation of tRNAs into the A site. Here, we show that thermorubin causes ribosomes to stall in vivo and in vitro at internal and termination codons.
evidence_notes: Characterized by Paranjpe et al. 2023 (Nucleic Acids Res 51:449-467; PMID:36546783) and Bulkley et al. 2012 (J Mol Biol 416:571-578; PMID:22240456; DOI:10.1016/j.jmb.2011.12.055) as a Thermoactinomyces antibioticus anthracenopyranone antibiotic that binds intersubunit bridge B2a of the bacterial 70S ribosome and inhibits Escherichia coli tolC-mutant growth (MIC ~1.6 ug/mL) and translation elongation/termination. Resolves the structureless ChEBI parent CHEBI:48516 (thermorubin) via the specific defined structure CHEBI:48480 (thermorubin A).
definition: A tetracyclic anthracenopyranone natural-product antibiotic from Thermoactinomyces antibioticus that binds bacterial 70S ribosomal intersubunit bridge B2a and arrests translation elongation and termination.

label: zafirlukast
evidence_snippet: Zafirlukast showed modest direct-acting antimicrobial activity (0.5-32 ug/mL) against a panel of Gram-positive bacteria, including MRSA. It was also found that Zafirlukast synergised with a number of existing antibiotics. Mutational analysis suggested the target of Zafirlukast in Staphylococci is LtaS (Lipoteichoic acid synthase).
evidence_notes: Reported by Siegwart et al. 2026 (Antibiotics 15:914; PMID:42792065) to exhibit direct antibacterial activity (MIC 0.5-32 ug/mL) against Gram-positive bacteria including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) via inhibition of lipoteichoic acid synthase (LtaS), in addition to antimycobacterial activity targeting nucleoid-associated protein Lsr2.
definition: An indole-based sulfonylcarbamate (leukotriene receptor antagonist) with direct anti-Gram-positive and antimycobacterial activity mediated by inhibition of staphylococcal lipoteichoic acid synthase (LtaS) and mycobacterial Lsr2.

label: (2R,3R)-dihydromyricetin
evidence_snippet: DMY exhibited significant antibacterial activity against GBS2, with a minimum inhibitory concentration and minimum bactericidal concentration of 0.5 mg/mL. Crystal violet staining and confocal laser scanning microscopy analyses demonstrated that DMY effectively inhibited and disrupted biofilm formation.
evidence_notes: Reported by Ma et al. 2026 (Foodborne Pathog Dis; PMID:42908502) as a natural dihydroflavonol (ampelopsin) with direct antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Streptococcus agalactiae (MIC = 0.5 mg/mL, MBC = 0.5 mg/mL) and synergy with beta-lactams, ciprofloxacin, and vancomycin.
definition: A (2R,3R)-3,3',4',5,5',7-hexahydroxyflavanone (ampelopsin) natural product with direct antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial pathogens.

label: 6-methylflavone
evidence_snippet: Among the compounds tested, 6-methylflavone (6-MF) was identified as a selective inhibitor of mycobacterial growth. 6-MF showed consistent activity against multiple clinical isolates of M. abscessus with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values of 8-16 ug/mL and was also effective against intracellular mycobacteria without cytotoxicity.
evidence_notes: Reported by Oh et al. 2026 (Microbiol Spectr; PMID:42007697) as a selective antimycobacterial flavone that disrupts mycobacterial membrane potential and respiratory energetics, inhibiting clinical Mycobacterium abscessus isolates at MIC 8-16 ug/mL and reducing pulmonary bacterial burden in vivo.
definition: A 6-methyl-2-phenyl-4H-chromen-4-one synthetic flavone with selective antimycobacterial activity against Mycobacterium abscessus via disruption of mycobacterial membrane energetics.

label: enterololin
evidence_snippet: Here we screened 10,747 bioactive small molecules for antibacterial activity against AIEC and discovered enterololin, an antibacterial compound with targeted activity against Enterobacteriaceae species. Molecular substructure- and deep learning-guided mechanism-of-action investigations revealed that enterololin perturbs lipoprotein trafficking through a mechanism involving the LolCDE complex, laboratory-evolved resistant mutants predominantly mapped to lolC and lolE, with an in vitro frequency of resistance of ~10-8 to 10-7.
evidence_notes: Reported by Catacutan et al. 2025 (Nat Microbiol 10:2827-2841; PMID:41044363) as a narrow-spectrum Enterobacteriaceae-selective antibacterial targeting the LolCDE lipoprotein transport complex (resistance mutations in lolC and lolE), active against adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (MIC ~2-4 ug/mL, and potentiated across multidrug-resistant Enterobacteriaceae with SPR741).
definition: A pyrazolyl-pyrimidinamine antibacterial agent that inhibits outer-membrane lipoprotein trafficking via the LolCDE complex in Enterobacteriaceae.

label: sorfequiline
evidence_snippet: TBAJ-876, a clinical development candidate of this series, shows attractive in vitro antitubercular activity and efficacy in a murine tuberculosis model. TBAJ-876 displayed submicromolar in vitro activity against reference strains representing the three subspecies of M. abscessus and against a collection of clinical isolates.
evidence_notes: Reported by Sarathy et al. 2020 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 64:e02404-19; PMID:31964791) and Sarathy et al. 2019 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 63:e01191-19; PMID:31358589; DOI:10.1128/aac.01191-19) as a next-generation 3,5-dialkoxypyridine diarylquinoline (TBAJ-876, INN sorfequiline) targeting the c and epsilon subunits of mycobacterial F1FO-ATP synthase, with MIC50 = 0.004 uM against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv and submicromolar MICs (0.15-0.6 uM) across Mycobacterium abscessus isolates.
definition: A 3,5-dialkoxypyridine diarylquinoline antimycobacterial agent (TBAJ-876) that inhibits mycobacterial F1FO-ATP synthase by binding both the c-ring and epsilon subunit.

label: CRS3123
evidence_snippet: Both exhibited potent antibacterial activity in the nanomolar range against multiple Enterococcus species, including vancomycin-resistant and vancomycin-sensitive E. faecium, E. faecalis, E. hirae, and E. durans. CRS3123 displayed exceptional potency, with MIC values of < 0.007 ug/mL for most strains.
evidence_notes: Reported by Abdelmegeed et al. 2025 (Sci Rep 15:44061; PMID:41413129) and Lomeli et al. 2019 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 63:e01395-19; PMID:31685472; DOI:10.1128/aac.01395-19) as a narrow-spectrum diaryldiamine inhibitor (REP3123) of bacterial type 1 methionyl-tRNA synthetase (MetRS), exhibiting MIC90 = 1 ug/mL against Clostridioides difficile and MIC < 0.007 ug/mL against vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium and Enterococcus faecalis.
definition: A (4R)-6,8-dibromochroman-4-ylamino-linked thieno[3,2-b]pyridin-7-one derivative (REP3123) that selectively inhibits bacterial type 1 methionyl-tRNA synthetase (MetRS) in Clostridioides difficile and Gram-positive cocci.

label: besifloxacin
evidence_snippet: Haas et al. evaluated the in vitro antibacterial activity of the novel 8-chloro-fluoroquinolone besifloxacin against 2,690 ocular clinical isolates and reported MIC90 values of 0.06 ug/mL against methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, 1 ug/mL against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, 0.06 ug/mL against Streptococcus pneumoniae, and 0.03 ug/mL against Haemophilus influenzae.
evidence_notes: Reported by Haas et al. 2009 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 53:3552-3560; PMID:19506065) and Cambau et al. 2009 (J Antimicrob Chemother 63:443-450; DOI:10.1093/jac/dkn528) as an 8-chloro-fluoroquinolone antibacterial (BOL-303224-A) with balanced inhibition of bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. PubChem CID 10178705 and ChEBI CHEBI:135622 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for besifloxacin.
definition: An 8-chloro-7-[(3R)-3-aminoazepan-1-yl]-1-cyclopropyl-6-fluoro-4-oxo-1,4-dihydroquinoline-3-carboxylic acid fluoroquinolone antibacterial that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

label: ozenoxacin
evidence_snippet: Tato et al. evaluated the nonfluorinated quinolone ozenoxacin (T-3912) against 1,031 Gram-positive clinical isolates from skin and soft tissue infections and reported MIC50 and MIC90 values of 0.002 and 0.004 ug/mL for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, 0.004 and 0.12 ug/mL for methicillin-resistant S. aureus, and 0.015 and 0.03 ug/mL for Streptococcus pyogenes.
evidence_notes: Reported by Tato et al. 2014 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 58:591-595; PMID:24080666) and Yamakawa et al. 2002 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 46:1229-1234; DOI:10.1128/AAC.46.5.1229-1234.2002) as a nonfluorinated pyridone quinolone antibacterial (T-3912) that dually inhibits DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV. PubChem CID 9863827 and ChEBI CHEBI:136050 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for ozenoxacin.
definition: A nonfluorinated 1-cyclopropyl-8-methyl-7-[5-methyl-6-(methylamino)pyridin-3-yl]-4-oxo-1,4-dihydroquinoline-3-carboxylic acid quinolone antibacterial that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

label: pazufloxacin
evidence_snippet: Fukuoka et al. evaluated the in vitro and in vivo antibacterial activities of T-3761 (pazufloxacin) and reported MIC90 values of 0.39 ug/mL against methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, 0.025 to 0.39 ug/mL against Enterobacteriaceae species, and 0.78 ug/mL against Pseudomonas aeruginosa, along with inhibition of Escherichia coli DNA gyrase supercoiling.
evidence_notes: Reported by Fukuoka et al. 1993 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 37:384-392; PMID:8460909) and Muratani et al. 1992 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 36:2293-2303; DOI:10.1128/AAC.36.10.2293) as a 10-(1-aminocyclopropyl) oxazine-ring-fused fluoroquinolone antibacterial (T-3761). PubChem CID 65957 and ChEBI CHEBI:94700 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for pazufloxacin.
definition: A (3S)-10-(1-aminocyclopropyl)-9-fluoro-3-methyl-7-oxo-2,3-dihydro-7H-[1,4]oxazino[2,3,4-ij]quinoline-6-carboxylic acid fluoroquinolone antibacterial that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV.

label: radezolid
evidence_snippet: Locke et al. evaluated the biaryl oxazolidinone radezolid (RX-1741) against Staphylococcus aureus strains and reported MIC values of 0.25 to 0.5 ug/mL against wild-type S. aureus ATCC 29213 and RN4220 and 1 to 4 ug/mL against linezolid-resistant strains carrying 23S rRNA mutations or the cfr methyltransferase gene.
evidence_notes: Reported by Locke et al. 2009 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 53:5265-5274; PMID:19752277) and Skripkin et al. 2008 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 52:3550-3557; DOI:10.1128/AAC.01193-07) as a biaryl-tetrazolylmethyl oxazolidinone antibacterial (RX-1741) targeting the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl transferase center. PubChem CID 11224409 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for radezolid.
definition: A biaryl oxazolidinone antibacterial agent (RX-1741) bearing a [(2H-tetrazol-5-ylmethyl)amino]methyl side chain that binds the bacterial 50S ribosomal subunit peptidyl transferase center and inhibits protein synthesis.

label: sutezolid
evidence_snippet: Williams et al. evaluated the thiomorpholinyl oxazolidinone PNU-100480 (sutezolid) against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv, reporting an MIC of 0.25 ug/mL (twofold lower than linezolid) and markedly superior sterilizing bactericidal activity in a murine tuberculosis model both alone and in combination with first-line antitubercular drugs.
evidence_notes: Reported by Williams et al. 2009 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 53:1314-1319; PMID:19075058) and Barbachyn et al. 1996 (J Med Chem 39:680-685; DOI:10.1021/jm950956y) as a thiomorpholinyl oxazolidinone antitubercular agent (PNU-100480, U-100480) that inhibits mycobacterial 50S ribosomal protein synthesis. PubChem CID 465951 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for sutezolid.
definition: A thiomorpholinyl oxazolidinone antimycobacterial agent (PNU-100480) that binds the 23S rRNA peptidyl transferase center of the mycobacterial 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibits bacterial translation.

label: cadazolid
evidence_snippet: Locher et al. characterized cadazolid (ACT-179811) against Clostridioides difficile strains including fluoroquinolone- and linezolid-resistant isolates, reporting an MIC50 of 0.125 mg/L and MIC90 of 0.25 mg/L, potent inhibition of C. difficile protein synthesis (IC50 0.08 to 0.31 mg/L), and inhibition of toxin and spore formation.
evidence_notes: Reported by Locher et al. 2014 (J Antimicrob Chemother 69:719-726; PMID:24128668) and Baldoni et al. 2014 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 58:901-908; DOI:10.1128/AAC.01789-13) as a hybrid oxazolidinone-fluoroquinolone antibacterial (ACT-179811, CAS 1025097-10-2) that primarily inhibits bacterial translation and weakly inhibits DNA gyrase in Clostridioides difficile. The IUPAC structure from DOI:10.1093/jac/dkt411 was normalized with RDKit to derive the standard InChI and InChIKey.
definition: A hybrid oxazolidinone-fluoroquinolone antibacterial agent (ACT-179811) that inhibits Clostridioides difficile protein synthesis at the 50S ribosomal subunit and DNA synthesis via DNA gyrase.

label: nilofabicin
evidence_snippet: Park et al. evaluated the 2-pyridone FabI inhibitor CG400549 (nilofabicin) against 209 clinical Staphylococcus aureus isolates (111 MSSA and 98 MRSA) and reported an MIC range of 0.06 to 1.0 mg/L with uniform MIC50 and MIC90 values of 0.25 mg/L, plus in vivo efficacy in murine systemic S. aureus infections.
evidence_notes: Reported by Park et al. 2007 (J Antimicrob Chemother 60:568-574; PMID:17606482) and Bogdanovich et al. 2007 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 51:4191-4196; DOI:10.1128/AAC.00501-07) as a selective 2-pyridone inhibitor (CG400549) of staphylococcal enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (FabI). PubChem CID 11844916 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for nilofabicin.
definition: A 1-(3-amino-2-methylbenzyl)-4-[2-(thiophen-2-yl)ethoxy]pyridin-2(1H)-one antibacterial agent (CG400549) that selectively inhibits staphylococcal enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (FabI).

label: sanfetrinem
evidence_snippet: Singh et al. tested the tricyclic beta-lactam (trinem) sanfetrinem (GV104326) against 287 Gram-positive organisms and reported MIC90 values of <=0.03 to 0.06 ug/mL for Streptococcus pyogenes, Streptococcus agalactiae, and penicillin-susceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae, 0.125 ug/mL for methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus, and 1 ug/mL for ampicillin-susceptible Enterococcus faecalis.
evidence_notes: Reported by Singh et al. 1996 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 40:2142-2146; PMID:8878596) and Di Modugno et al. 1994 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 38:2362-2368; DOI:10.1128/AAC.38.10.2362) as a broad-spectrum tricyclic carbapenem/trinem beta-lactam antibiotic (GV104326) with high stability to beta-lactamases and potent activity against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, anaerobic, and mycobacterial pathogens. PubChem CID 71452 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for sanfetrinem.
definition: A tricyclic beta-lactam (trinem) antibacterial agent (GV104326) that acylates bacterial penicillin-binding proteins and L,D-transpeptidases to inhibit peptidoglycan cross-linking.

label: tomopenem
evidence_snippet: Koga et al. evaluated the novel parenteral 1-beta-methylcarbapenem CS-023 (RO4908463, tomopenem) against Gram-positive and Gram-negative clinical isolates and reported MIC90 values of 4 ug/mL against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, 0.25 ug/mL against penicillin-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae, <=0.06 ug/mL against Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae, and 2 ug/mL against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
evidence_notes: Reported by Koga et al. 2005 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 49:3239-3250; PMID:16048932) as a 2-guanidinylacetylamino-pyrrolidinylthio 1-beta-methylcarbapenem antibiotic (CS-023, RO4908463) that binds penicillin-binding proteins including PBP2a of MRSA and PBPs of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. PubChem CID 9809656 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for tomopenem.
definition: A parenteral 1-beta-methylcarbapenem beta-lactam antibiotic (CS-023, RO4908463) bearing a guanidinylacetylamino-pyrrolidinylthio side chain that inhibits bacterial penicillin-binding proteins including MRSA PBP2a.

label: PC190723
evidence_snippet: Haydon et al. reported that the difluorobenzamide derivative PC190723 inhibited cell division FtsZ GTPase activity in a concentration-dependent manner (IC50 = 55 ng/mL), exhibited potent bactericidal activity against all tested Staphylococcus strains including methicillin- and multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus at MICs of 0.5 to 1.0 ug/mL, and cured mice in a lethal S. aureus septicemia model.
evidence_notes: Reported by Haydon et al. 2008 (Science 321:1673-1675; PMID:18801997) as a 3-[(6-chloro[1,3]thiazolo[5,4-b]pyridin-2-yl)methoxy]-2,6-difluorobenzamide antibacterial that binds the interdomain cleft of the bacterial cytokinetic protein FtsZ and blocks Z-ring constriction. PubChem CID 25016417 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for PC190723.
definition: A 2,6-difluorobenzamide thiazolopyridine antibacterial agent that allosterically binds the interdomain cleft of staphylococcal cell division protein FtsZ and blocks cytokinesis.

label: TXA707
evidence_snippet: Kaul et al. designed the metabolic-stability-optimized FtsZ-targeting benzamide TXA707 by replacing the Cl atom of PC190723 with a CF3 group and reported bactericidal activity against methicillin-resistant, vancomycin-intermediate, and linezolid-resistant Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolates with MIC values of 0.5 to 2 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: Reported by Kaul et al. 2015 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 59:4835-4844; PMID:26033735) and Kaul et al. 2017 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 61:e00863-17; DOI:10.1128/AAC.00863-17) as the active FtsZ-targeting 2,6-difluorobenzamide antibacterial moiety of the prodrug TXA709. PubChem CID 90135655 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for TXA707.
definition: A 2,6-difluoro-3-{[6-(trifluoromethyl)[1,3]thiazolo[5,4-b]pyridin-2-yl]methoxy}benzamide antibacterial agent (active moiety of TXA709) that targets staphylococcal cell division protein FtsZ.

label: BTZ043
evidence_snippet: Makarov et al. discovered 1,3-benzothiazin-4-ones and identified the S-enantiomer BTZ043, reporting an MIC of 1 ng/mL (2.3 nM) against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv and 4 ng/mL against Mycobacterium smegmatis, covalent inhibition of decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-epimerase (DprE1), and bactericidal efficacy across multidrug- and extensively drug-resistant M. tuberculosis clinical isolates.
evidence_notes: Reported by Makarov et al. 2009 (Science 324:801-804; PMID:19299584) as the first-in-class 8-nitro-6-(trifluoromethyl)-1,3-benzothiazin-4-one antitubercular agent (BTZ-043) that undergoes nitroreduction and forms a covalent semimercaptal adduct with Cys387 of mycobacterial DprE1. PubChem CID 42609849 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for BTZ043.
definition: A 2-[(2S)-2-methyl-1,4-dioxa-8-azaspiro[4.5]decan-8-yl]-8-nitro-6-(trifluoromethyl)-4H-1,3-benzothiazin-4-one antitubercular agent that covalently inactivates mycobacterial decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-oxidase (DprE1).

label: TBA-7371
evidence_snippet: Shirude et al. identified 1,4-azaindole noncovalent inhibitors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-epimerase (DprE1) and reported that compound 8 (TBA-7371, AZ-7371) inhibited M. tuberculosis DprE1 with an IC50 of 10 nM, inhibited M. tuberculosis H37Rv growth with an MIC of 1.56 uM (0.55 ug/mL), and reduced bacterial load in acute and chronic murine tuberculosis infection models.
evidence_notes: Reported by Shirude et al. 2013 (J Med Chem 56:9701-9708; PMID:24215368) and Shirude et al. 2014 (ACS Med Chem Lett 5:792-796; PMID:24957839; DOI:10.1021/ml500134b) as a clinical-stage 1,4-azaindole noncovalent DprE1 inhibitor (TBA-7371, AZ-7371). PubChem CID 72792692 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and SMILES for TBA-7371.
definition: A 1,4-azaindole (N-(2-hydroxyethyl)-1-[(6-methoxy-5-methylpyrimidin-4-yl)methyl]-6-methyl-1H-pyrrolo[3,2-b]pyridine-3-carboxamide) antitubercular agent that noncovalently inhibits mycobacterial decaprenylphosphoryl-beta-D-ribose 2'-oxidase (DprE1).

label: SQ109
evidence_snippet: Tahlan et al. demonstrated that the 1,2-ethylenediamine antitubercular clinical candidate SQ109 inhibits Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv growth at an MIC of 0.39 to 0.78 ug/mL (1.2 to 2.4 uM) and blocks trehalose monomycolate export by targeting the inner-membrane transporter MmpL3 (Rv0206c), causing trehalose monomycolate accumulation and loss of trehalose dimycolate and cell wall mycolates.
evidence_notes: Reported by Tahlan et al. 2012 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 56:1797-1809; PMID:22252828) and Protopopova et al. 2005 (J Antimicrob Chemother 56:968-974; DOI:10.1093/jac/dki319) as an N-geranyl-N'-(2-adamantyl)ethane-1,2-diamine antimycobacterial agent targeting MmpL3 and proton-motive-force bioenergetics. PubChem CID 5274428 supplies the neutral parent standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for SQ109.
definition: An N-geranyl-N'-(adamantan-2-yl)ethane-1,2-diamine antimycobacterial agent that inhibits the mycobacterial trehalose monomycolate transporter MmpL3 and dissipates the transmembrane proton motive force.

label: negamycin
evidence_snippet: Olivier et al. determined the crystal structure of negamycin bound to the Escherichia coli 70S ribosome, showed that negamycin binds helix 34 of the 30S ribosomal subunit head domain to induce translational stalling and miscoding (translation IC50 = 1.8 uM), and reported an MIC of 32 ug/mL against E. coli ATCC 25922 and single-rrn strain SQ110 that increased 16- to 32-fold upon 16S rRNA U1052G or U1060A mutation.
evidence_notes: Reported by Olivier et al. 2014 (Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 111:16274-16279; PMID:25368144) and Polikanov et al. 2014 (Mol Cell 56:541-550; DOI:10.1016/j.molcel.2014.09.021) as a Streptomyces pseudodipeptide hydrazide antibiotic targeting 16S rRNA helix 34 in the 30S ribosomal decoding center. PubChem CID 11118411 and ChEBI CHEBI:198310 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for negamycin.
definition: A natural pseudodipeptide hydrazide antibiotic ([2-[(3R,5R)-3,6-diamino-5-hydroxyhexanoyl]-1-methylhydrazinyl]acetic acid) that binds helix 34 of the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit to impair translocation and induce miscoding.

label: amicoumacin A
evidence_snippet: Polikanov et al. solved the 2.4 A crystal structure of amicoumacin A bound to the Thermus thermophilus 70S ribosome, showing that amicoumacin A bridges 16S rRNA bases in the E-site of the 30S subunit and the mRNA backbone to block translocation, and demonstrated that 16S rRNA mutations C795U, A794G, or G693A increase the Escherichia coli Delta-tolC MIC from 0.5-1 ug/mL to 4-8 ug/mL.
evidence_notes: Reported by Polikanov et al. 2014 (Mol Cell 56:531-540; PMID:25306919) and Lama et al. 2012 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 56:2802-2807; DOI:10.1128/AAC.00147-12) as a Bacillus dihydroisocoumarin natural-product antibiotic (MIC 0.25-0.78 ug/mL against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus) that stabilizes mRNA in the 30S ribosomal E-site. PubChem CID 25223631 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for amicoumacin A.
definition: A Bacillus-derived 3,4-dihydroisocoumarin-pseudopeptide antibiotic that binds the 30S ribosomal subunit E-site to tether mRNA to 16S rRNA and inhibit bacterial translation translocation.

label: bactobolin A
evidence_snippet: Chandler et al. identified quorum-sensing-controlled bactobolin A as the broad-spectrum antibiotic secreted by Burkholderia thailandensis, reported an MIC of 0.31 ug/mL against Bacillus subtilis 168, and demonstrated that resistance mutations map to the conserved uL2 (RplB) ribosomal protein (E236A or E236Q, increasing the B. subtilis MIC to 4.2 to 5.0 ug/mL).
evidence_notes: Reported by Chandler et al. 2012 (mBio 3:e00499-12; PMID:23249812) and Amunts et al. 2015 (J Mol Biol 427:753-755; DOI:10.1016/j.jmb.2014.12.018) as a Burkholderia thailandensis polyketide-peptide hybrid antibiotic that binds a unique site on the 50S ribosomal subunit coordinated by ribosomal protein uL2 and 23S rRNA together with P-site tRNA. PubChem CID 54676871 and ChEBI CHEBI:138579 supply the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for bactobolin A.
definition: A Burkholderia thailandensis dichloromethyl bicyclic lactone-alanine hybrid antibiotic that binds the bacterial ribosome at the P-site tRNA/23S rRNA/ribosomal protein uL2 interface and inhibits translation termination.

label: opelconazole
evidence_snippet: Colley et al. characterized PC945 (opelconazole) as a novel inhaled triazole inhibitor of Aspergillus fumigatus sterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51A IC50 = 0.23 uM; CYP51B IC50 = 0.22 uM) and reported an MIC50 of 0.032 ug/mL and MIC90 of 0.064 ug/mL across 96 clinical A. fumigatus isolates.
evidence_notes: Reported by Colley et al. 2017 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 61:e02280-16; PMID:28223388) and Rudramurthy et al. 2019 (J Antimicrob Chemother 74:2943-2951; DOI:10.1093/jac/dkz280) as a lung-retention-optimized triazole antifungal (PC945) targeting fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51A/CYP51B) across Aspergillus and Candida species. PubChem CID 121383526 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for opelconazole.
definition: A long-acting inhaled triazole antifungal agent (PC945) that inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51A/CYP51B) and blocks ergosterol biosynthesis in Aspergillus and Candida species.

label: quilseconazole
evidence_snippet: Lockhart et al. evaluated the fungal-CYP51-specific tetrazole inhibitor VT-1129 (quilseconazole) against 180 Cryptococcus neoformans and 251 Cryptococcus gattii clinical isolates and reported MIC50 and MIC90 values of 0.015 and 0.06 ug/mL against C. neoformans and 0.06 and 0.25 ug/mL against C. gattii, including fluconazole-resistant strains.
evidence_notes: Reported by Lockhart et al. 2016 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 60:2528-2531; PMID:26787697) and Warrilow et al. 2016 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 60:4530-4538; DOI:10.1128/AAC.00349-16) as a selective 1-tetrazole antifungal agent (VT-1129) that tightly binds Cryptococcus neoformans and Cryptococcus gattii sterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51, Kd = 11 to 14 nM). PubChem CID 91886002 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for quilseconazole.
definition: A 1-tetrazole antifungal agent (VT-1129) that selectively coordinates the heme iron of fungal sterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51) to inhibit ergosterol biosynthesis in Cryptococcus and Candida species.

label: albaconazole
evidence_snippet: Carrillo and Guarro evaluated the novel quinazolinone triazole UR-9825 (albaconazole) against Scedosporium apiospermum and Scedosporium prolificans isolates, reporting geometric mean MICs of 0.30 ug/mL against S. apiospermum (MIC90 = 1 ug/mL) and 1.18 ug/mL against S. prolificans (MIC90 = 2 ug/mL), the lowest values among all four triazoles tested.
evidence_notes: Reported by Carrillo and Guarro 2001 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 45:2151-2153; PMID:11408242) and Ramos et al. 1999 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 43:2992-2994; DOI:10.1128/AAC.43.12.2992) as a broad-spectrum 7-chloroquinazolin-4(3H)-one triazole antifungal agent (UR-9825) inhibiting fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51), with MIC90 <= 0.06 ug/mL against Candida albicans and Cryptococcus neoformans. PubChem CID 208952 supplies the standard InChI, InChIKey, formula, and isomeric SMILES for albaconazole.
definition: A 7-chloro-3-[(1R,2R)-2-(2,4-difluorophenyl)-2-hydroxy-1-methyl-3-(1H-1,2,4-triazol-1-yl)propyl]quinazolin-4(3H)-one triazole antifungal agent (UR-9825) that inhibits fungal lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase (CYP51).
